Certain plants are labeled weeds by human beings and are thus deserving of death by chemical means. And the film shows us how effectively Dow insecticides blast them off this mortal coil for good. Granted, some of the plants shown are genuinely problematic, but the strident note of this film gets to you after awhile. Like some of the fly control films made at the same time, you start to feel a sense that the bright, clean 50s world could only exist through diligent efforts to…

The whole line of Dow's new weed killers are shown in 'Death To Weeds', a boring infomercial designed to wow farmers on how 'safe' the chemicals, such as d-44, were to your plant and animals. It pretty much follows this standard.. A state is shown, an overgrown field is shown, then the spraying, and the effect after it's done. Fairly numbing.

rv: The final reel in the 4 series, offers no surprises here.. First clip is of a travelling barber who goes to trailer park to trailer park. No doubt to offer all the inbred kids a hand. We then see a clip of an unusual train/bus combo. Looks like an interesting idea, wonder why something like that isn't used today (like for remoter areas) We then see.. Yes! A firefighting dog! He rides along with the firemen ringing the bell, and dangerously climbing a ladder to rescue a girl's DOLL (???!!). Why? Who knows. We don't see the dog flying down the pole though (as shown with the firefighting kitten…

(Sigh!) More silly news stories from Chevrolet. Theres a traveling barber that serves trailer folk, a combination bus-train, more animal abuse in the form of a fire dog that gets sent into flames to rescue a little girls dolly, an early version of eye-in-the-sky traffic reports, and model boat races. (Sigh!) I need to go to bed now Ratings: Camp/Humor Value: ***. Weirdness: ***. Historical Interest: ****. Overall Rating: ***.
